name: freckle-mcp
description: Build company and people lists, enrich leads, author and run Workflows, import HubSpot and Salesforce records, monitor Signals and sync Ads audiences in Freckle, through Freckle's hosted MCP server.

interface.longDescription:
Freckle is a lead enrichment and GTM data platform for sales, marketing and RevOps teams. This plugin lets ChatGPT and Codex work in your Freckle Workspace through Freckle's hosted MCP server:

- Find companies and people with AI Ark or Apollo searches, preview the matches, then build Lists.
- Fill work emails, phone numbers and company details through provider waterfalls, and score or route rows.
- Author, run and schedule Workflows over Workbook Datasets, and report their results.
- Import HubSpot and Salesforce records, pasted rows or CSV files into Datasets.
- Monitor Signals such as job openings, new hires and job changes.
- Sync Datasets to LinkedIn, Meta and Google Ads audiences.
- Check the Workspace, credit balance, usage and connections.

You need a Freckle account. You sign in with OAuth, and the plugin acts only in Workspaces you belong to. List runs, enrichment and Signals use the Workspace's Freckle credits: the plugin states the cost and asks before spending them. Integration secrets are entered only in Freckle's browser form, never in chat. Buying credits, changing plans and deleting an account or Workspace are not available through the plugin.
capabilities: Preview and build company and people lists from AI Ark and Apollo searches
Find work emails, phone numbers and company details through provider waterfalls
Enrich, score and route leads in Workbook Datasets
Import pasted rows and CSV files into Datasets
Author, run and change Workflows, with a cost quote and approval before credits are spent
Monitor Signals for job openings, new hires and job changes
Sync Datasets to LinkedIn, Meta and Google Ads audiences
Report on Workbooks, Datasets and Workflow runs
Check the Workspace, credit balance and credit usage
Connect integrations through Freckle's browser form
defaultPrompt: Find 100 RevOps leaders at US SaaS companies and verify their emails.
Import HubSpot companies missing a domain or key contact, then find the missing domains and decision-makers.
Find US fintech companies that raised funding in the last 90 days, find their Head of Sales and verify their email address.

positive.description: Read-only check of the connected Workspace and its credit balance.
positive.prompt: Which Freckle Workspace am I connected to, and how many credits do I have left?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the current Workspace and the user's role, lists any other Workspaces the user can switch to, and reports the current credit balance. Makes no changes and spends no credits.

positive.description: Preview a people search for an ideal customer profile, with a sample and the match count, without creating a List or spending credits.
positive.prompt: Find VPs of Sales at US software companies with 50 to 500 employees. Show me a sample and how many match, but don't build the list yet.
positive.tools_triggered: listBuilds_getAIArkFilters, listBuilds_getFilterValues, listBuilds_previewAIArkPeople (listBuilds_previewPeople instead when Apollo is the recommended provider)
positive.expected_behavior: Recommends a provider (AI Ark or Apollo) and says why, runs one preview with those filters, and shows up to 10 matching people (name, title, company) with the total number of matches and the estimated credit cost of building the List. Creates no List and spends no credits. Offers to build the List and waits for a yes on the quoted cost before any create or run.

positive.description: Create a Workbook from three pasted company domains and fill in company details, quoting the credit cost and waiting for approval before any credits are spent.
positive.prompt: Create a Workbook called Review Test with these companies: stripe.com, notion.so, figma.com. Fill in industry, employee count and HQ country for each.
positive.tools_triggered: workspace_context, creditUsage_getCurrentCredits, workbooks_createWorkbook, datasets_createWorkbookDataset, datasets_importDatasetCsv, workflowNodes_listWorkflowNodes, workflowNodes_getWorkflowNodes, workflowDrafts_getDraftSyntax, workflows_buildWorkflow, datasets_triggerWorkflowDatasetConnection, workflowRuns_wait, datasets_listDatasetEntries (in Codex with file access, workflowDrafts_initDraft and workflows_createDraftUploadUrl take the place of workflows_buildWorkflow)
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the Review Test Workbook with exactly 3 rows, then builds and connects an enrichment Workflow without running it (building is free). Before any run, states the maximum credit cost (a few credits for 3 rows) against the balance and asks for a yes. After the yes, runs the 3 rows, waits for them to finish, and reports industry, employee count and HQ country for each company, any gaps, and the credits actually used. Without a yes, nothing runs and no credits are spent.

positive.description: Read-only explanation of the managed LinkedIn URL to Enriched Profile + Work Email Workflow: its input, steps, providers, outputs and credit cost.
positive.prompt: Explain how the LinkedIn URL to Enriched Profile + Work Email workflow works: what I give it, what I get back, and what it costs.
positive.tools_triggered: workflowNodes_listWorkflowNodes, workflows_getWorkflow, workflows_listWorkflowNodes (workflowNodes_getWorkflowNodes for provider details)
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the managed Workflow by name and explains it from the live definition: the input is one LinkedIn profile URL; it enriches the profile through a provider waterfall (such as AI Ark, LeadMagic and HarvestAPI), finds a work email through a waterfall (such as AI Ark, Hunter, Findymail, LeadMagic and Dropcontact) and validates it with ZeroBounce; it returns the email, whether it is valid, full name, company domain, the profile and email sources, the ZeroBounce status and a failure reason when none is found. States the maximum cost (about 5.67 credits per row) and that a row with no billable result costs nothing. Runs nothing, changes nothing and spends no credits.

positive.description: Build and import a capped lookalike company List from one seed domain, quoting the credit cost and waiting for approval before the import runs.
positive.prompt: Build a list of 25 US companies similar to gusto.com with 50 to 1,000 employees. Call it Review Lookalikes.
positive.tools_triggered: listBuilds_getAIArkFilters, listBuilds_previewAIArkCompanies, listBuilds_createAIArkCompanies, listBuilds_run, listBuilds_get, datasets_listDatasetEntries
positive.expected_behavior: Runs one AI Ark company preview with gusto.com as the lookalike seed, US location, 50 to 1,000 employees and a cap of 25, then shows up to 10 sample companies, the total number of matches and the estimated credit cost of importing 25. Asks for a yes before creating or running anything. After the yes, creates the Review Lookalikes List capped at 25, runs it, waits for the import to finish, and reports the number of companies saved (at most 25) with a short sample and the credits used. Without a yes, nothing is created and no credits are spent.

negative.description: Purchases are out of scope: the plugin exposes no billing or payment tools, so it must not buy credits or charge a card.
negative.prompt: Buy 5,000 more Freckle credits and charge my card on file.
negative.tools_triggered: None that change state. It may read workspace_context or creditUsage_getCurrentCredits to show the current balance.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines to buy credits or charge a card and says purchases are not available through the plugin; plans and credit options are described at https://www.freckle.io/pricing and managed in the Freckle app. Charges nothing and calls no state-changing tool.

negative.description: Deleting a Freckle account or Workspace is irreversible and not exposed through the MCP server; the plugin must not attempt it or bulk-delete data instead.
negative.prompt: Delete my Freckle account and everything in it.
negative.tools_triggered: None. No delete or archive tool is called.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines: there is no tool to delete a Freckle account or Workspace, and it won't bulk-delete the Workspace's data. Points the user to Freckle support for account deletion, and offers to archive specific Workbooks the user names, each after confirmation. Deletes and archives nothing.

negative.description: Data in a Workspace the signed-in user doesn't belong to can't be accessed.
negative.prompt: Show me the Workbooks in Acme Corp's Freckle Workspace.
negative.tools_triggered: workspace_context only. If workspace_select is tried, the server answers forbidden: "You are not a member of that Workspace."
negative.expected_behavior: Checks the user's Workspaces, says Acme Corp isn't one of them and can't be accessed, and shows no data from it. Never passes another organization's ID to other tools; if a switch is attempted, it is refused and the plugin stops.

review.commerce_description: Freckle doesn't sell products or process payments in ChatGPT or Codex. Some actions use the Workspace's existing Freckle credits; the plugin states the cost and asks before spending them. Credits and plans are managed outside the plugin, in the Freckle app.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.0: first directory release of Freckle. Build company and people lists, enrich leads, author and run Workflows, import HubSpot and Salesforce records, monitor Signals and sync Ads audiences through Freckle's hosted MCP server, with a cost quote and approval before credits are spent.
